Subject: Duplicate sentence fragments showing up in generated summaries

Hi Ben,

We've observed a small subset of responses from the Redwood API that contain duplicated sentence fragments — e.g. the model will output the same short sentence twice in a row near the end of a summary. This started showing up in a few runs yesterday after we switched to the newer model checkpoint (redwood/sf-3b-v2).

I've attached a small sample (sample_output.json) that includes three examples and the request IDs. We see it ~0.4% of the time across ~8k requests. Can you please investigate whether this is a server-side artifact or something on our end?

Example snippet from sample_output.json:
---
"...Our analysis indicates that the policy is sound. Our analysis indicates that the policy is sound."
---

Thanks — Samir

Subject: Investigation summary — duplication claim (INF-7234)

Hi Samir — thanks again for the sample and patience while we investigated. Summary of what we did and what we found: 

1) Replays and log review (platform): we replayed the request IDs from sample_output.json against redwood/sf-3b-v2 in the same region and runtime configuration you reported. We were unable to reproduce the duplicated sentence in any of the replays (n=12 replays per request). Platform logs show a single generation stream per request and no duplicated append operations. Audit logs do not show retries or double-submits for the affected request IDs.

2) Model artifact check (research): checked the sf-3b-v2 checkpoint and tokenization behavior; no evidence of duplicated training artifacts that would systematically emit repeated short sentences. Per-replica sampling traces look normal.

3) Correlation with streaming: one of the customer traces used streaming=true. In the logs we observed a short reconnect from the client at ~2.1s in that session (client-side socket re-open). If a client replays the final prompt fragment after a dropped stream, client-side concat logic can produce what appears to be a repeated sentence in the final concatenated output. 

Conclusion: We did not find a platform-side root cause. The most likely explanation is client-side behavior — either a prompt re-send after a streaming reconnect, or a post-processing step that concatenates partial fragments without de-duplicating. That said, we keep INF-7234 open for 7 days to watch for other reports and will re-open if reproducible evidence appears.

What we attached: debug_logs.txt (server-side sampling traces and request headers for the replayed requests) and reproduction_commands.sh (commands we used to replay requests).

Suggested next steps for Novum: 
- Replay asserts on the client with streaming=false for a sample set and compare outputs.
- If you must use streaming, add an idempotency token or server-generated cursor to avoid double-appends; consider deduping final concatenated fragments on the client.
- If you'd like, we can schedule a 60-minute joint debugging session (engineer-to-engineer) where we tail live traces and reproduce with your real prompts — we can offer up to 2 hours free for this triage.

As a courtesy for the time spent on this investigation, I'm happy to extend a $500 invoice credit to your account if this helps. Please let me know if you want the debug session scheduled and what time zones work — I have windows tomorrow morning PT and early afternoon PT.

If anything changes on your side or you capture reproducible examples that include raw prompts and request headers, please re-open the ticket or reply-all here.

Best,
